# chronosphere_query_resource_pools (Resource)

Singleton grouping of automated metric query sources (monitors, recording rules, SLOs, and service accounts) into named pools, each with a data read limit that rejects the pool's queries when sustained. This resource is backed by Chronosphere's unstable config API and is subject to breaking change without notice.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `default_pool` (Block List, Max: 1) Catch-all pool that receives query sources not matched by any other pool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--default_pool))
- `pool` (Block List) Pools that group automated query sources. Query sources map to the first pool that matches, in declaration order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--pool))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedblock--default_pool"></a>
### Nested Schema for `default_pool`

Optional:

- `data_read_limit` (Block List, Max: 1) Data read limit enforced on the pool. Omit to leave the pool unlimited. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--default_pool--data_read_limit))

<a id="nestedblock--default_pool--data_read_limit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `default_pool.data_read_limit`

Required:

- `max_datapoints_read_per_second` (Number) Maximum datapoints read per second for the pool, aggregated across all sources in the pool. A value of `0` blocks all queries from the pool.

Optional:

- `sustain_secs` (Number) How long the pool must remain above `max_datapoints_read_per_second` before its queries are rejected. Must be a whole multiple of 60 seconds, between 60 and 300; `0` (or omitted) applies the 60-second default. Must be omitted when `max_datapoints_read_per_second` is `0`, which rejects queries immediately.



<a id="nestedblock--pool"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pool`

Required:

- `name` (String) Unique name of the pool.
- `source_types` (List of String) Source types that map to this pool: `MONITOR`, `RECORDING_RULE`, `SLO`, or `SERVICE_ACCOUNT`. A query source maps to the first pool whose `source_types` matches its source type and whose `source_names` (if set) matches its source name.

Optional:

- `data_read_limit` (Block List, Max: 1) Data read limit enforced on the pool. Omit to leave the pool unlimited. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--pool--data_read_limit))
- `source_names` (List of String) Narrows the pool to specific named sources of the pool's source types: service account IDs for `SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, monitor slugs for `MONITOR`, recording rule slugs for `RECORDING_RULE`, and SLO slugs for `SLO`.

<a id="nestedblock--pool--data_read_limit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `pool.data_read_limit`

Required:

- `max_datapoints_read_per_second` (Number) Maximum datapoints read per second for the pool, aggregated across all sources in the pool. A value of `0` blocks all queries from the pool.

Optional:

- `sustain_secs` (Number) How long the pool must remain above `max_datapoints_read_per_second` before its queries are rejected. Must be a whole multiple of 60 seconds, between 60 and 300; `0` (or omitted) applies the 60-second default. Must be omitted when `max_datapoints_read_per_second` is `0`, which rejects queries immediately.
